title: Device Placement and Memory Limits
summary: Review device placement, batch-size limits and live-allocation memory evidence.

steps.title: Place models and tensors on the correct compute device

blocks.text: An accelerator label does not establish placement. Verify availability and the devices of the model, features and targets.

Check torch.cuda.is_available() before selecting torch.device("cuda"); otherwise use the supported CPU device. Move the model with model.to(device) and each feature and target tensor with tensor.to(device). Inspect parameter and minibatch devices, then check the declared placement with a bounded forward/backward fixture.

Assert valid, boundary and failure predicates; false predicates raise AssertionError in ordinary non-optimized execution. Only for the authorized supplied VM, gcloud compute instances start INSTANCE --zone=ZONE and gcloud compute instances stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE change lifecycle state. Wait and inspect the result. gcloud compute ssh INSTANCE --zone=ZONE connects to the running authorized VM for the workload.

before.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
model = nn.Linear(2, 1)
features = torch.tensor([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]])
targets = torch.tensor([[1.], [2.]])
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
features = features.to(device)  # Model and targets have not yet been moved.
before_devices = ([p.device for p in model.parameters()], features.device, targets.device)
before_same_device = all(p.device == features.device == targets.device
                         for p in model.parameters())
# CPU fallback may already align them; inspect rather than assume a mismatch.

after.code:
model = model.to(device)
features = features.to(device)
targets = targets.to(device)
after_devices = ([p.device for p in model.parameters()], features.device, targets.device)
same_device = (all(p.device == features.device == targets.device for p in model.parameters()) and features.device.type == device.type)
assert same_device
model.zero_grad()
outputs = model(features)
loss = nn.MSELoss()(outputs, targets)
loss.backward()
bounded_execution_ok = (outputs.shape == targets.shape
                        and loss.shape == torch.Size([])
                        and bool(torch.isfinite(loss))
                        and all(p.grad is not None and bool(torch.isfinite(p.grad).all())
                                for p in model.parameters()))
assert bounded_execution_ok

blocks.text: The authorized lifecycle procedure and tensor placement are separate checks. Inspect instance identity and state before acting. Select CUDA only after checking availability, otherwise record the supported CPU path. Move and inspect the model, features and targets together; moving only features is insufficient. Check the bounded forward/backward fixture. After the workload, stop the authorized instance, wait and verify its state. Record actual placement rather than copying the intended hardware label.
A running VM does not prove tensor placement. Verify availability, compatible devices and the bounded fixture; stop and verify the authorized VM afterward.

public.prompt: Read the authorized-VM lifecycle and device-placement excerpts. Decide whether each meets its stated criterion. INSTANCE and ZONE denote the same authorized instance throughout; both CUDA-available and supported CPU fallback paths are checked. Classify every supplied excerpt; judge the criterion named in that excerpt.

items.text:
```text
gcloud compute instances describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE
# Check authorized identity and initial stopped state.
gcloud compute instances start INSTANCE --zone=ZONE
# Wait; describe same instance and verify RUNNING.
gcloud compute ssh INSTANCE --zone=ZONE
# After bounded work:
gcloud compute instances stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE
# Wait; describe same instance and verify TERMINATED.
```
Placement portion:
```python
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model.to(device)
features = features.to(device)
targets = targets.to(device)
assert next(model.parameters()).device == features.device == targets.device
outputs = model(features)
loss = loss_fn(outputs, targets)
loss.backward()
# Prediction uses the same placed fixture; no repeated transfers.
record = (device, next(model.parameters()).device, features.device, targets.device)
```
Tests cover available CUDA, unavailable CUDA with supported CPU, and a deliberately false device-equality predicate that must raise AssertionError in ordinary non-optimized execution.
Model and features are on cuda; targets remain on cpu. The placement assertion is deleted and the report says placement is compatible.
cuda.is_available is false, but the reviewer selects cuda solely because the planned option is an accelerator.
After the stop command, no wait or describe occurs; the lifecycle report assumes stopped state.

i1.message: Identity and lifecycle states are checked around authorized actions; availability governs selection and all operands are placed and inspected together before the bounded computation.

i2.message: All model, feature and target operands must use compatible devices; deleting the assertion does not repair placement.

i3.message: The supported CPU fallback is required when CUDA availability is false.

i4.message: The resulting stopped state and identity require verification, not an assumption from issuing a command.

steps.title: Adjust training batch size to fit available memory

blocks.text: A larger batch may improve throughput but must satisfy the declared memory bound. Input bytes are only an estimate.

Training memory includes other live allocations; larger batches ordinarily require more activation storage. Change only DataLoader batch_size, keeping alignment and the task fixed. For each CUDA trial, reset_peak_memory_stats() before the workload and inspect torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() afterward for peak allocated tensor bytes.

That peak does not cover every component of GPU usage: use the quantity governed by the supplied budget. Compare completed work per elapsed time among eligible sizes. Estimate features as batch_rows × feature_columns × bytes_per_feature_element, add targets under their own dtype, and compare the estimate with the measured peak.

steps.title: Batch-size trials against the declared memory bound

blocks.text: Inspect the registered batch-size trials rather than equating feature-plus-target bytes with total training memory. Keep the task, alignment and measurement protocol fixed. Reset each CUDA trial’s peak before measuring; otherwise an earlier peak can contaminate the comparison. Record actual batch shapes, including the partial final batch, with completed examples and elapsed time. Higher throughput does not rescue a setting outside the declared memory bound. Select only among settings meeting the supplied requirements.
Allocated-tensor peak is not total GPU usage. Input-byte estimates omit other live allocations; eligibility must follow the declared measured-memory scope.

items.text:
```python
torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
# Same bounded training task, with actual batch counts retained.
# Synchronize at elapsed-time boundaries.
peak = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()
```
Review computes features as rows × columns × feature-element bytes and adds target bytes under the target dtype. It retains the final partial count, uses actual completed examples/time, filters completed settings by the stated budget and minimum throughput, and selects batch_size=100. Input estimates are not treated as total training peaks.
Review selects batch_size=200 solely for its highest throughput, despite peak=46000 and budget=30000.
The input estimate is below the budget, so the reviewer declares every trial eligible without consulting peak allocated tensor bytes.
A final partial batch is counted as one full batch_size when calculating completed examples/time.
The CUDA peak is never reset between batch-size trials; each stored value is treated as that trial’s own peak.

i1.message: This uses the intended peak quantity and actual completed work, distinguishes input estimates from other allocations and selects the highest eligible throughput.

i2.message: Higher throughput does not rescue a setting outside the measured memory bound.

i3.message: Feature-plus-target bytes are not peak training memory and do not establish eligibility.

i4.message: Throughput must count actual completed examples, including the smaller final batch.

i5.message: An earlier trial’s peak can contaminate the comparison without a reset before each measured workload.

blocks.text: Locate the failure: distinguish occupied tensors, reserved storage and retained graphs.

CUDA memory_allocated measures tensor-occupied memory; memory_reserved includes caching-allocator storage. Inspect peak allocated and reserved memory and the failure point. Graph-connected saved tensors can retain graph memory; use detached or scalar diagnostics when gradients through saved values are unnecessary.

empty_cache releases unused cache, not storage occupied by live tensors. Test one supported change, such as smaller batches or removing an unnecessary graph reference, on the same bounded workload; verify completion and peak. Count each parameter, gradient, activation and batch matrix as element_count × element_width, summing simultaneously live allocations rather than inputs alone.

steps.title: Live allocations: parameters are not total memory

blocks.text: Use the supplied linear-layer widths to count weight and bias elements separately. Apply each allocation’s element width, then include simultaneously live gradients, activations and batch matrices. At the reproduced failure, inspect allocated/reserved evidence and saved graph-connected diagnostics. Test one supported correction on the same bounded workload and compare completion and measured peak with the failed reference. Do not sum every tensor ever created or treat a smaller successful task as the same comparison.
empty_cache cannot release live tensor storage. Reserved differs from allocated, and the input matrix alone does not explain training memory.
